{{short description|Thai mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=April 2022}}
'''Ngamta''' "'''"Natalie"'''" '''Thamwattana''' is a Thai mathematician who works in Australia as a Professor of Applied Mathematics at the [[University of Newcastle (Australia)]].<ref name="profile">[https://www.newcastle.edu.au/profile/natalie-thamwattana], University of Newcastle, retrieved 2018-10-8.</ref> In 2014 she won the J. H. Michell Medal of [[ANZIAM]] for her "pioneering contributions in the areas of granular materials and nanotechnology".<ref name="Michell">{{citation|url=https://www.austms.org.au/Publ/Gazette/2014/Mar14/ANZIAM.pdf|work=ANZIAM awards|title=Winner of the 2014 J.H. Michell Medal|accessdate=2016-10-13}}</ref>

Thamwattana came from [[Chumphon Province]] in Thailand, where her mother made dresses and her father worked in the police.
After her first year of university, her high test scores in science and mathematics earned her a government scholarship with full tuition and, later, support for doctoral studies abroad.<ref name="odds">{{citation|title=Against the odds: A young, village girl from Thailand, with a passion for mathematics proved that it doesn't matter where you come from, you can change the world|first=Keeli|last=Cambourne|publisher=[[University of Wollongong]]|accessdate=2016-10-13|url=http://stand.uow.edu.au/against-the-odds/}}</ref>
She earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from [[Mahidol University]] in Thailand in 2000, choosing mathematics because as a mathematician she wouldn't "have to play with the chemical stuff and we didn't have to kill rat or any insects".<ref name="profile"/> She completed her Ph.D. at Wollongong in 2004 under the supervision of James Murray Hill.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=146221}}</ref>

After completing her studies, she returned the money from her Thai scholarship in order to stay in Australia with her new husband, a lecturer at Wollongong.<ref name="odds"/> She joined the Wollongong faculty herself, and founded the Nanomechanics Group there.<ref name="Michell"/> In 2018 she moved to [[University of Newcastle (Australia)]] to take up a position as professor of Applied Mathematics.
